articles.title: Elias Vasquez, 67, Tailor
articles.deck: Friends remember Elias Vasquez for the many years of service to Kettle Hill.
body: Born in Kettle Hill in the years after the war, Elias Vasquez spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood. Elias Vasquez died in March at home on Orion Terrace, at the age of 67.
Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Kettle Hill.

Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Eastgate Senior Lunch Program in his or her name. Born in Kettle Hill in the years after the war, Elias Vasquez spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood.

articles.title: Letters: Pine Road Parking Is Out of Control
body: To the editor: Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed.

To the editor: I have lived on Pine Road for 33 years, and I want to say what a difference the Mill Hill Lions Club has made. I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the September meeting.

articles.title: Scout Troop 14 Opens Bike Repair Clinic on Briar Lane
articles.deck: The work is expected to take 37 weeks and will be paid for with $12,000 raised locally.
body: The group has raised $12,000 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food.

The effort began in December when a handful of neighbors met at Millrace Green to talk about bike repair clinic. Organizers say the work is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Friday mornings.

Dominic Pelletier, who has lived on Briar Lane for 37 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected. The Hickory Ridge Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.

articles.title: Zoning Board Hears Plan for Sidewalk Ramp Near Lower Millrace
articles.deck: The vote came after 23 residents spoke at Saturday’s session.
body: Public works estimates the work will take about 23 weeks once it starts in June.

Councilmember Alma Weatherby asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $25,000. Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.
The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first.
